text:
evan: Heads-up—I'm planning a controlled switchover from ClusterIP->NLB for the inference-gateway svc this week. Goal: move TLS passthrough to NLB while keeping existing ALB for canary users. Quick QA on the plan?

nina: +1 to a canary. main concerns: healthchecks (probe port binding) and secretbinding namespace scope. Did you plan to change targetPort or keep it?

evan: Keeping targetPort the same (grpc 8081). We'll add a NodePort for the NLB and set externalTrafficPolicy: Local so source IP preserved. Probe remains on 8081. Terraform change is small: add aws_lb_target_group + nodeport mapping.

raj: Watch out for probe routing when externalTrafficPolicy:Local — if pods aren't on every node probes can fail during gradual rollout. Suggest: set readiness gate to drain first, or use additional pod anti-affinity to spread.

evan: Good call. Plan is: 1) terraform apply NLB TG + TargetGroupBinding; 2) deploy new Service with nodePort + annotation for proxy-protocol off; 3) canary traffic by adjusting Route weight in gateway; 4) monitor traces/401s for TLS handshake.

sydney: On secrets: the NLB passthrough requires the cert on the target (we're doing tcp passthrough) — are we reusing the same k8s TLS secret or creating per-namespace binding? If we create a new secret in kube-system it may break secretbinding controllers.

evan: Intend to reuse the existing tls/inference-gw secret in infra namespace. But we need to ensure the Gateway's SecretBinding references that secret (not the ALB-specific secret). I have a terraform snippet: ```resource "kubernetes_secret" "inference_tls" { metadata { name = "inference-gw-tls" namespace = "infra" } data = { tls.crt = filebase64("${path.module}/certs/gw.crt") tls.key = filebase64("${path.module}/certs/gw.key") } }```

nina: If you're using TargetGroupBinding, note that some clusters expect the secret in the same namespace as the Service. We had a hit/miss previously. Recommend adding a copy step in the deploy job: copy secret to svc namespace before canary.

raj: Also check the NLB healthcheck protocol — for gRPC we use TCP on 8081. AWS will mark unhealthy quickly if app-level readiness isn't set. Consider using an HTTP health endpoint on a different port (readiness).

evan: We'll add a readiness probe on /ready (HTTP 8082) that returns 200 when KV cache warm and model ready. NLB TG will keep using TCP 8081, ALB stuck can hit 8082 if we need app-level checks.

sydney: Timing window? I can help with secret copy job and monitoring runbook.

evan: Plan to do canary Tuesday 02:00 UTC (low traffic). Will open a short incident channel and pager on-call for 2 hours. CI pipeline will run terraform plan and an automated smoke deploy job: `make infra-plan && ci-bot apply-if-approved`.

deploy-bot: CI pipeline queued: infra/terraform#782 plan started. Waiting for approvals from @nina or @raj.

nina: I can review the TF plan this morning. Quick question — will you enable connection draining on the ALB side for overlap?

evan: Yes, enable deregistration_delay (300s) on ALB target groups to allow in-flight requests to complete during the weight shift. NLB side will have connection_termination disabled so we rely on app drain.

raj: Sounds good. I recommend a post-migration check-list message: confirm secret binding, confirm probe success on >=3 nodes, confirm latency SLOs, and verify logs for TLS handshake errors.

evan: Will post checklist and attach terraform diff. Thanks all — pinging again when plan is up for approval. :thumbsup:
